name: PoLyInfo (NIMS Polymer Database)
description: NIMS database of polymer properties extracted from scientific literature, covering ~100 property classes (thermal, electrical, mechanical) with chemical structures, monomers, polymerization and processing conditions. Holds ~19,000 homopolymers, ~175,000 polymer samples and ~552,000 property data points from ~22,000 literature sources. Manually curated; bulk download is prohibited.
license: NIMS MatNavi Terms (free registration; bulk download prohibited)
associated_paper: Ishii et al., 'NIMS polymer database PoLyInfo (I)', Sci. Technol. Adv. Mater.: Methods 4 (2024)

name: Khazana / Polymer Genome (Ramprasad Group)
description: Khazana is a searchable repository of downloadable published computational materials data (DFT datasets for polymers and dielectrics) with ML utilities; Polymer Genome is the associated polymer property-prediction platform trained on DFT and experimental literature data. Thousands of polymer/organic-material property records for polymer informatics.
associated_paper: Kim et al., 'Polymer Genome: A Data-Powered Polymer Informatics Platform', J. Phys. Chem. C 122 (2018)

name: CoRE MOF Database (Computation-Ready, Experimental MOFs)
description: Curated set of ~14,000 computation-ready experimental metal-organic framework crystal structures (2019 release) derived from the CSD and literature, with solvent removed and disorder resolved for direct use in simulation. Includes computed pore analytics (LCD, PLD, surface area, void fraction); distributed as CIFs and CSVs on Zenodo.
associated_paper: Chung et al., 'CoRE MOF 2019', J. Chem. Eng. Data 64 (2019)

name: QMOF Database
description: Database of quantum-chemical properties (band gaps, charges, electronic structure) for 20,000+ metal-organic frameworks and coordination polymers, generated by high-throughput periodic DFT. Downloadable from Figshare and explorable via the Materials Project MOF Explorer.
associated_paper: Rosen et al., 'Machine Learning the Quantum-Chemical Properties of MOFs', Matter 4 (2021)

name: hMOF (Hypothetical MOF Database)
description: Database of ~137,000 hypothetical MOF structures generated by recombining building blocks (Wilmer et al. 2012), with GCMC-simulated gas adsorption isotherms (CH4, CO2, H2, N2, Xe/Kr) and textural properties. Hosted and distributed in bulk through MOFX-DB at Northwestern.
associated_paper: Wilmer et al., 'Large-scale screening of hypothetical metal-organic frameworks', Nat. Chem. 4 (2012)

name: CSD MOF Subset (Cambridge Structural Database)
description: CCDC-curated subsets of the CSD identifying ~100,000+ MOF/coordination-polymer entries, updated with each CSD release. Full access requires a CSD licence, but a freely accessible collection of 10,636 CIFs of 3D non-disordered porous MOFs (solvent removed) is provided for research use.
license: CCDC/CSD licence; free MOF CIF collection for research
associated_paper: Moghadam et al., 'Development of a Cambridge Structural Database Subset: MOFs', Chem. Mater. 29 (2017)

name: MOFX-DB
description: Searchable database (Snurr group, Northwestern) of ~160,000 MOF and zeolite structures aggregated from CoRE MOF, hMOF, ToBaCCo, IZA and other sources, with millions of pre-computed GCMC adsorption isotherms for CH4, CO2, H2, N2, Xe, Kr and H2O plus textural properties. Bulk downloads and a REST API.
associated_paper: Bobbitt et al., 'MOFX-DB: An Online Reference Database', J. Chem. Eng. Data (2023)

name: CURATED COFs
description: Hundreds of experimentally reported covalent-organic framework crystal structures collected from the literature with git-tracked corrections, paper provenance and CIFs. DFT-optimized structures with DDEC charges are published on Materials Cloud for adsorption screening.
associated_paper: Ongari et al., 'Building a Consistent and Reproducible Database for Adsorption Evaluation in COFs', ACS Cent. Sci. 5 (2019)

name: SciGlass (open release via EPAM)
description: Formerly commercial glass property database released openly on GitHub: property data for ~422,000 glass compositions (oxide, halide, chalcogenide) compiled from 40,000+ literature sources and patents, plus ~15,000 optical spectra and 3,800 ternary glass-formation diagrams. Distributed as Microsoft Access (.mdb) files.

name: INTERGLAD Ver. 8 (International Glass Database System)
description: International Glass Database System (New Glass Forum, Japan) with property and structural data for ~405,000 glasses compiled from literature, patents and manufacturer catalogs, plus property-prediction and composition-optimization tools. Paid licence; limited free trial after registration.

name: NIMS MatNavi (incl. Creep/Fatigue/Corrosion Data Sheets)
description: NIMS Materials Database platform spanning polymer, inorganic and metallic databases, notably the NIMS Structural Materials Data Sheets: decades-long creep, fatigue, corrosion and space-use strength test series on steels and alloys. Free after DICE registration; bulk download prohibited.
license: NIMS MatNavi Terms (free registration; bulk download prohibited)

name: Expanded MPEA Dataset (Borg et al., high-entropy alloys)
description: Literature-compiled dataset of mechanical properties (hardness, yield strength, elongation) and observed phases for 630 multi-principal element / high-entropy alloys, from papers published through 2020. Machine-readable files on Figshare accompanying a Scientific Data descriptor.
associated_paper: Borg et al., 'Expanded dataset of mechanical properties and observed phases of MPEAs', Sci. Data 7, 430 (2020)

name: RRUFF Project Database
description: Integrated database of high-quality Raman spectra, X-ray powder diffraction patterns, infrared spectra and measured chemistry for thousands of well-characterized mineral samples, measured at the University of Arizona from documented specimens. A reference standard for mineral identification.
associated_paper: Lafuente et al., 'The power of databases: the RRUFF project', in Highlights in Mineralogical Crystallography (2015)

name: NIST X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Database (SRD 20)
description: Critically evaluated collection of over 22,000 XPS line positions, chemical shifts, doublet splittings and energy separations of photoelectron and Auger-electron lines, compiled from published literature (v5.0, updated 2023). Interactive search by element, line type and energy.

name: MAGNDATA (Bilbao Crystallographic Server)
description: Collection of more than 2,000 published commensurate and incommensurate magnetic structures (mostly from neutron diffraction), described with magnetic space/superspace group symmetry and downloadable as magCIF files compatible with VESTA, Jmol, JANA and FullProf.
associated_paper: Gallego et al., 'MAGNDATA: towards a database of magnetic structures. I.', J. Appl. Cryst. 49 (2016)

name: HOPV15 (Harvard Organic Photovoltaic Dataset)
description: Experimental photovoltaic performance data (HOMO/LUMO, PCE, Voc, Jsc) from the literature for ~350 organic donor molecules, paired with quantum-chemical calculations over multiple conformers using several DFT functionals. An experiment-theory calibration resource for organic electronics; on Figshare.
associated_paper: Lopez et al., 'The Harvard organic photovoltaic dataset', Sci. Data 3, 160086 (2016)

name: OCELOT Database (Organic Crystals in Electronic and Light-Oriented Technologies)
description: Open archive (Risko group, Univ. Kentucky) of 56,000+ experimentally determined organic semiconductor crystal structures from ~47,000 distinct molecules, enriched with high-throughput DFT-computed optoelectronic descriptors and ML tools. Web interface and Python API.
associated_paper: Ai et al., 'OCELOT: An infrastructure for data-driven research on organic semiconductors', J. Chem. Phys. 154 (2021)

name: NIST TRC ThermoML Archive
description: Archive of experimental thermophysical, thermochemical and transport property data in the IUPAC-standard ThermoML XML format, produced by the NIST Thermodynamics Research Center in cooperation with five major journals. Machine-readable files carry data points with uncertainties, methods and full bibliographic metadata.
associated_paper: Frenkel et al., 'XML-based IUPAC standard (ThermoML)', Pure Appl. Chem. 78 (2006)

name: NIST AM Bench (Additive Manufacturing Benchmark Test Series)
description: NIST-led series of highly controlled additive manufacturing benchmark measurements (2018/2022/2025) for validating AM process simulations: laser powder bed fusion of Ni superalloys and stainless steel, DED and polymer AM, with in-situ melt-pool, microstructure, residual strain and mechanical data. Permanently archived for public use with blind modeling challenges.
associated_paper: AM Bench measurement papers, Integrating Materials and Manufacturing Innovation
